Hi Emma —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we covered
- Scope: BrightCart product search & recommendations workflow, 100k monthly users, latency target <150ms for NLU paths.
- Current pain: semantic mismatch in recommendations after the June model update; saw measurable drop in click-through on category-expansion queries.
- What you need from Redwood: model recommendations that improve topical relevance, clear evals/benchmarks, and a safe rollback path in case of regressions.

Immediate next steps (my proposed timeline)
1) Share our benchmark export (attached) with your core prompts and metrics — DONE (evaluation_benchmarks_v2.csv).
2) Redwood to suggest 2 model variants and a prompt set tuned for your taxonomy by EOD Jul 9.
3) Technical deep-dive with engineering to review diffs and rollback options — propose Jul 10 or 11.

Notes on the attached: the CSV includes the prompt set you shared plus our eval metrics (precision@1, recall, semantic-similarity scores) and a small diff of outputs between v2026-05-30 and v2026-06-25.

If that looks right, I'll schedule the deep-dive and loop in our inference leads.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Quick assessment after scanning the CSV and running the prompt set locally: 

Findings
- The diff column shows a consistent drop in semantic-similarity for ~18% of category-expansion prompts between v2026-05-30 and v2026-06-25. Topline signal looks credible.
- Latency is unchanged; CPU/GPU footprint of the newer variant is similar, so rollback should not materially change rate-limit capacity.

Recommendation
1) Immediate: implement a 10% canary back to v2026-05-30 for 48 hours focused on category-expansion route only. This limits customer impact and gives clear A/B signal.
2) Parallel: run the candidate variants we discussed (quantized-medium and dense-small) against the full prompt set overnight and push the updated benchmark CSV to the shared Drive link.
3) If canary shows >5% relative uplift in precision@1 and no latency regressions, expand rollout; else perform full rollback to v2026-05-30.

Rollback playbook (short)
- Pin route to v2026-05-30 (API-level config change) — takes ~10 minutes to enact, instant effect.
- Monitor errors/latency for 30 minutes.
- If stable, keep pinned and schedule a broader rollback communication with PM/legal.

I've attached a short playbook and a sanity checklist. Rishi — can you validate the timeline and confirm the config change steps?

Monica
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
